description:
Roll a release out to a fleet in waves. The plan is `/work/rollout.json`, a JSON object `{"release": STRING, "waves": [[HOST, ...], ...]}`: the release to deploy and a list of waves, each a list of host names.

Start the deploy of each host with `deploy_start` (`svc.deployStart` in TypeScript), passing the host and the plan's release, with a 1 second timeout on each call. A call that fails, for any reason, means that host failed; never retry a deploy, since starting one twice is not safe.

- Waves run in plan order. A wave starts only after every call of the previous wave has answered or timed out.
- Within a wave, run up to two deploys at once: there are never more than two calls in flight, and while a wave still has hosts waiting, two calls are in flight. Every host of a wave is attempted, even when another host of the same wave fails.
- A host may appear more than once in the plan. Only its first appearance counts; ignore the later ones. A wave left with no hosts is complete at once.
- If any host of a wave failed, start no later wave. The hosts of the waves that were not started are skipped.

Print one line to standard output: a JSON object with three fields. `deployed` is a list of `{"host": HOST, "revision": REVISION}` objects, one per host whose deploy started, with the revision the service returned. `failed` is a list of `{"host": HOST, "kind": KIND}` objects, one per failed host, where `KIND` is the failure kind (`Timeout`, `Unavailable`, `RateLimited`, `NotFound`, `PermissionDenied`, `Invalid`, `Conflict`, or `Failed`). `skipped` is the list of skipped host names. Every list is in plan order, by each host's first appearance, and holds each host once.

Exit with status 0 when no host failed, and 4 otherwise.

Started.doc: A deploy that has started on a host.

capabilities.description: Starts deploying the release on one host and returns the revision it was given.
